name: Poliquin Step-Up / Heel-Elevated Lateral Step-Up
description: The Poliquin step-up is a unilateral exercise developed to specifically target the vastus medialis (VMO). The lifter steps sideways onto a low box or step while keeping the working heel elevated, maximizing knee extension load on the inner quadriceps. The heel-elevated foot position prevents weight shifting to the hip extensors, making this a highly specific VMO strengthening exercise used extensively in knee rehabilitation and sports performance.

execution.starting_position: Stand beside a box or step approximately 4-6 inches high. Place the working foot on the step laterally, with the heel elevated slightly (by the step edge or a plate beneath the heel). The opposite foot remains on the floor.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a low step or box. Place heel on the edge to create slight elevation. Begin with bodyweight.
steps: Step 1: Drive the working heel down into the step, extending the knee from roughly 90 degrees to full extension.
Step 2: At no point does the opposite foot leave the floor or take weight — it is a touch guide only.
Step 3: Lower back down with control, allowing the knee to flex back to about 90 degrees.
Step 4: Repeat all reps on one side before switching.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on extension, inhale on the controlled return.
common_mistakes: Pushing through the floor foot rather than the step foot
Full knee extension with a lock-out that reduces tension
safety_considerations: Very low-load exercise — appropriate for post-surgery rehabilitation when cleared
Consult a physiotherapist if using for patellar tracking issues
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Work from approximately 90 degrees of knee flexion to nearly full extension. Keep tension on the VMO throughout.
coaching_cues: Drive through the heel of the step foot only
No weight on the floor foot
